verdict.line: You lose if you let him stick on you in melee before you're Mega; you win once Trinity Force comes online and you start chaining mega-form stun combos.

brief.thesis: Aatrox's Deathbringer Stance passive and E (Umbral Dash) both heal him off champion damage, so every extended trade or all-in before you reach Mega Gnar is tilted his way — that's why OP.GG marks lane and solo-kill advantage to him despite Gnar's 52.6% win rate over 268 games. Your edge isn't the laning phase, it's surviving it: mini Gnar's 1100-range Q (Boomerang Throw) lets you poke and slow without trading into his sustain, and your actual power comes online once Rage fills W (Wallop) into a stun and your Trinity Force/Black Cleaver timing outpaces his two heal sources.

theirWindow.what: Umbral Dash heals him whenever it damages a champion, so if it's up he can dash onto you, trade, and sustain the damage back. Disengage to max Q range and let him hit minions instead until it's spent.

yourWindow.when: You're Mega Gnar with W up
yourWindow.what: Mega form's W (Wallop) stuns in an area — land it first, then E (ground-slam area damage), then pick up your Q boulder for the slow. This is the only sequence where your burst outpaces both his passive and E healing.

start.why: Highest-performing start in this matchup (50.6% over 235 games, 70.4% pick) — the extra damage and sustain let mini Gnar win the poke war instead of standing in melee range.

boots.why: Dominant pick (49.3% over 278 games, 87.4% pick) — flat damage reduction blunts his empowered Deathbringer Stance autos and basic Q/E poke.

core.why: Part of the highest-winning core path (57.7% over 26 games) — the move speed and proc damage power your W (Hyper) kiting and mega combo burst.
Armor shred closes the gap against his two heal sources by making every hit, including mega E and R, do more.
Survivability spike that lets you stand in mega form combos without getting all-in'd back by his R-extended healing.

situational.when: his Deathbringer Stance/E healing is swinging fights back in his favor
you're ahead and want attack speed plus magic damage to shred through his armor-stacked build
you're behind and need armor and tenacity to survive his all-in windows

runes.keystoneWhy: The move speed and sustain on hit help you kite out of his E (Umbral Dash) range and reset neutral positioning between pokes; master-tier Gnar players instead run Lethal Tempo (54.1% win rate across 1,985 games) for the attack-speed scaling, which suits a more aggressive, duel-focused playstyle once you're comfortable all-inning off mega form.

summoners.why: This combo has the best measured win rate in the matchup (50.6% over 23.5% of games) — Ignite directly cuts into the healing that defines Aatrox's power in this lane (Deathbringer Stance and E's heal-on-damage), turning his sustain-based all-ins into losing trades.

playing.title: Poke in mini form, never melee
playing.detail: Use Q (Boomerang Throw)'s 1100 range and slow to chip him down before you're Mega. Walking into melee range lets his empowered auto and E sustain win the exchange.

playing.title: Track Rage, don't force all-ins
playing.detail: Mini Gnar has no stun and loses extended fights outright. Only commit once your Rage bar is close to full and a mega transform is imminent.

playing.title: Trade right after his E lands
playing.detail: His E (Umbral Dash) heals him on champion damage with a 9/8/7/6/5s cooldown. Engage in the window right after he's used it, not while it's up.

playing.title: Don't E through his Q stacks or W
playing.detail: OP.GG flags that his third Darkin Blade swing or a landed Infernal Chains can interrupt your E (Hop). Path around his Q count instead of hopping through it.

playing.title: Stun first, then combo
playing.detail: Once Mega, land W (Wallop)'s stun before anything else, then E for area damage, then pick up the Q boulder for the slow. Autoing first wastes the window.

playing.title: Build into the sustain race
playing.detail: Trinity Force into Black Cleaver into Sterak's Gage is your highest-winning path. The armor shred is what finally lets your damage catch his two heal sources.

playing.title: Ignite the engage
playing.detail: Pop Ignite the moment he commits his E or Q chain so his Deathbringer Stance/E healing can't fully offset the damage you're putting on him.

brief.patchCaveat: Build paths, rune pages, summoner spells, and win rates above are measured from live OP.GG games on the current patch; the mechanical reasoning, timing windows, and trade patterns are my own tactical read on why those numbers look the way they do.

stats.opponentTip: His third (Q) or (W) can be used to interrupt [E]. Be careful when avoiding his skills as you focus on contesting and farming lane.
